title: Triggers, Masonry, Proximity, Relight & Morph
description: A once-only CSS scroll trigger, a CSS-only masonry formula, cursor-proximity type, a WebGL relightable surface, and a button-to-toast spring morph.

drops.title: CSS Animation Triggers
drops.description: Discrete, once-only scroll entrances via the new timeline-trigger / animation-trigger CSS properties — never re-scrubs on scroll-back.
drops.concept: Scroll-driven animation-timeline: view() ties an animation's progress directly to scroll position, which is great for parallax but reads as oozy for entrances. The new CSS Animation Triggers spec (timeline-trigger + animation-trigger) instead fires a normal, eased keyframe animation exactly once when an element crosses an activation range, with a play-once action that locks the finished state on scroll-back. This drop implements the real CSS property where supported and a feature-detected IntersectionObserver fallback with byte-for-byte the same keyframes everywhere else.
drops.source: Michelle Barker — CSS Animation Triggers: Playing animations on scroll without scrubbing (utilitybend.com)

interaction.mouse: Scroll down to fire each card's entrance once
interaction.click: Replay button resets and scrolls back to the top
interaction.touch: Scrolling on mobile fires the same once-only entrances

drops.title: CSS-Only Row-Span Masonry
drops.description: A single grid-row: span calc() formula per card, derived from its own aspect ratio — no JS layout pass, no library.
drops.concept: True masonry packing usually needs a JS measurement pass (real column-balancing libraries) or the still-Safari-only native Grid Lanes. This technique instead computes each card's grid-row-end span directly from its own aspect ratio and a shared 'precision' constant — span = round((height/width) * precision) — so denser rows naturally stagger into a masonry look purely from CSS Grid's auto-placement, with zero measured pixel heights and zero hydration flicker.
drops.source: dangreen — Masonry Grid Goes CSS-Only: An Experimental Approach (dev.to)

interaction.mouse: Precision and column-width sliders retune the packing live
interaction.click: Reshuffle regenerates the deck with new aspect ratios
interaction.touch: Grid reflows the same way on any screen size

drops.title: Cursor-Proximity Type
drops.description: Letters swell in weight, width and glow the closer your cursor gets, driven by one live CSS custom property per glyph.
drops.concept: Instead of a JS library recomputing full styles per frame, this pattern keeps the interpolation in CSS: a per-letter --prox custom property (0 far, 1 close) is written once per frame from a plain distance calculation, and every visual response — font-variation-settings weight/width, a translateY lift, a color-mix shift toward the accent, and a glow — reads that single variable through calc() and color-mix(). It's the same 'CSS does the tweening, JS only feeds one number' idea behind the emerging pure-CSS proximity techniques built on view-timeline and sibling-index().
drops.source: Temani Afif — Hover Proximity with Scroll-Driven Animations (css-tip.com)

interaction.mouse: Move across any line — nearby letters swell and glow
interaction.click: Radius and max-weight sliders retune the falloff
interaction.touch: Auto-sweeps on touch devices to demonstrate the effect

drops.title: Cursor-as-Light-Source Relighting
drops.description: A flat depth map turns into a relightable surface — move your cursor and it becomes the light, with real per-pixel shadows.
drops.concept: A per-pixel depth (height) map lets a fragment shader derive synthetic surface normals from the local height gradient, then light them with a Lambertian term where the light direction is driven live by pointer position — the cursor doesn't move a DOM element, it becomes a physical light raking across the surface. A short heightfield raymarch toward the light direction adds real self-shadowing wherever a taller ridge blocks the light. Three procedurally generated depth scenes (embossed coin, ridges, orb cluster) stand in for the AI-estimated depth maps of the original.
drops.source: Dominik Fojcik — Relighting Images with Depth Maps and Three.js (Codrops)

interaction.mouse: Move over the surface — it becomes the light source
interaction.touch: Drag a finger across the surface to relight it

drops.title: Button-Becomes-Toast Morph
drops.description: Click a button and it clones its own shape as a toast, then springs into a stacking deck — shared-element motion, not slide-in.
drops.concept: Instead of the usual slide/fade toast, the pressed button's exact rect, radius, and background are read via getBoundingClientRect() and used as the toast's very first frame — so the toast looks like the button itself traveled there. Two independent underdamped springs (semi-implicit Euler) drive position and size on different timings, so size settles quickly while position keeps drifting — a timing gap that reads as physical weight. Older toasts scale down and peek behind the newest, fanning into a full list on hover.

interaction.mouse: Click any button to launch its own toast; hover the stack to fan it out
interaction.touch: Tap buttons and the stack works identically on mobile
